sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato dhātrī tatra gatvā śarmiṣṭhāṃ vākyam abravīt uttiṣṭha bhadre śarmiṣṭhe jñātīnāṃ sukham āvaha
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Then the nurse went there and spoke these words to Śarmiṣṭhā: "Arise, noble Śarmiṣṭhā, bring happiness to your kinsmen."

sanskrit: tyajati brāhmaṇaḥ śiṣyān devayānyā pracoditaḥ sā yaṃ kāmayate kāmaṃ sa kāryo 'dya tvayānaghe
english: "The brahmin, urged on by Devayānī, is abandoning his pupils. Whatever desire she holds, that must be fulfilled by you today, O sinless one."

sanskrit: śarmiṣṭhovāca sā yaṃ kāmayate kāmaṃ karavāṇy aham adya tam mā tv evāpagamac chukro devayānī ca matkṛte
english: Śarmiṣṭhā said: "Whatever desire she holds, I will fulfill it today. But let not Śukra and Devayānī depart on my account."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ kanyāsahasreṇa vṛtā śibikayā tadā pitur niyogāt tvaritā niścakrāma purottamāt
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Then, surrounded by a thousand maidens and carried in a palanquin, she swiftly departed from that foremost city by her father's command.

sanskrit: śarmiṣṭhovāca ahaṃ kanyāsahasreṇa dāsī te paricārikā anu tvāṃ tatra yāsyāmi yatra dāsyati te pitā
english: Śarmiṣṭhā said: "I, along with a thousand maidens, will be your servant and attendant. I will follow you wherever your father gives you in marriage."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca stuvato duhitā te 'haṃ bandinaḥ pratigṛhṇataḥ stūyamānasya duhitā kathaṃ dāsī bhaviṣyasi
english: Devayānī said: "You are the daughter of one who is praised and receives tribute, while I am the daughter of one who praises and renders tribute. How then can you become my servant?"

sanskrit: śarmiṣṭhovāca yena kena cid ārtānāṃ jñātīnāṃ sukham āvahet atas tvām anuyāsyāmi yatra dāsyati te pitā
english: Śarmiṣṭhā said: "By whatever means one can bring happiness to afflicted kinsmen — for that reason I will follow you wherever your father gives you in marriage."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pratiśrute dāsabhāve duhitrā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ devayānī nṛpaśreṣṭha pitaraṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Vaiśampāyana said: When the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan had thus promised her state of servitude, Devayānī, O best of kings, spoke these words to her father:

sanskrit: praviśāmi puraṃ tāta tuṣṭāsmi dvijasattama amoghaṃ tava vijñānam asti vidyābalaṃ ca te
english: "I am entering the city, father; I am satisfied, O best of twice-born ones. Your wisdom is unfailing, and your power of learning is immense."

sanskrit: evam ukto duhitrā sa dvijaśreṣṭho mahāyaśāḥ praviveśa puraṃ hṛṣṭaḥ pūjitaḥ sarvadānavaiḥ
english: Thus addressed by his daughter, that best of twice-born men of great renown entered the city with joy, honored by all the demons.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca atha dīrghasya kālasya devayānī nṛpottama vanaṃ tad eva niryātā krīḍārthaṃ varavarṇinī
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Then, after a long time, O best of kings, the fair-complexioned Devayānī went out to that very forest for sport.

sanskrit: tena dāsīsahasreṇa sārdhaṃ śarmiṣṭhayā tadā tam eva deśaṃ saṃprāptā yathākāmaṃ cacāra sā tābhiḥ sakhībhiḥ sahitā sarvābhir muditā bhṛśam
english: Together with that thousand servant-maids and with Śarmiṣṭhā, she reached that very place and wandered there at will, greatly delighted, accompanied by all those companions.

sanskrit: krīḍantyo 'bhiratāḥ sarvāḥ pibantyo madhumādhavīm khādantyo vividhān bhakṣyān vidaśantyaḥ phalāni ca
english: All of them were happily sporting, drinking honey-wine, eating various delicacies, and biting into fruits.

sanskrit: punaś ca nāhuṣo rājā mṛgalipsur yadṛcchayā tam eva deśaṃ saṃprāpto jalārthī śramakarśitaḥ
english: And once again King Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, arrived at that very spot by chance, seeking game, thirsting for water, and wearied by exertion.

sanskrit: dadṛśe devayānīṃ ca śarmiṣṭhāṃ tāś ca yoṣitaḥ pibantīr lalamānāś ca divyābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ
english: He saw Devayānī and Śarmiṣṭhā and those women drinking and frolicking, adorned with divine ornaments.

sanskrit: upaviṣṭāṃ ca dadṛśe devayānīṃ śucismitām rūpeṇāpratimāṃ tāsāṃ strīṇāṃ madhye varāṅganām śarmiṣṭhayā sevyamānāṃ pādasaṃvāhanādibhiḥ
english: And he saw the pure-smiling Devayānī seated among those women, incomparable in beauty, the finest of women, being waited upon by Śarmiṣṭhā with foot-massage and other services.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca dvābhyāṃ kanyāsahasrābhyāṃ dve kanye parivārite gotre ca nāmanī caiva dvayoḥ pṛcchāmi vām aham
english: Yayāti said: "Each of you is attended by a thousand maidens. I ask you both your family lineages and names."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca ākhyāsyāmy aham ādatsva vacanaṃ me narādhipa śukro nāmāsuraguruḥ sutāṃ jānīhi tasya mām
english: Devayānī said: "I will tell you — receive my words, O lord of men. Śukra is his name, the preceptor of the demons; know me as his daughter."

sanskrit: iyaṃ ca me sakhī dāsī yatrāhaṃ tatra gāminī duhitā dānavendrasya śarmiṣṭhā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ
english: "And this one is my companion and servant, who goes wherever I go — Śarmiṣṭhā, daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, lord of the demons."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca kathaṃ nu te sakhī dāsī kanyeyaṃ varavarṇinī asurendrasutā subhru paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: Yayāti said: "How can this maiden of fair complexion, the daughter of the lord of demons, be your companion and servant, O fair-browed one? I am greatly curious about this."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca sarva eva naravyāghra vidhānam anuvartate vidhānavihitaṃ matvā mā vicitrāḥ kathāḥ kṛthāḥ
english: Devayānī said: "Everything follows the ordinance of fate, O tiger among men. Understanding this as decreed by fate, do not weave strange tales about it."

sanskrit: rājavad rūpaveṣau te brāhmīṃ vācaṃ bibharṣi ca kiṃnāmā tvaṃ kutaś cāsi kasya putraś ca śaṃsa me
english: "Your form and dress are like a king's, yet you speak with a brahmin's speech. What is your name, where do you come from, and whose son are you? Tell me."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca brahmacaryeṇa kṛtsno me vedaḥ śrutipathaṃ gataḥ rājāhaṃ rājaputraś ca yayātir iti viśrutaḥ
english: Yayāti said: "Through brahmacharya the entire Veda has entered the path of my hearing. I am a king and a king's son, known by the name Yayāti."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca kenāsy arthena nṛpate imaṃ deśam upāgataḥ jighṛkṣur vārijaṃ kiṃ cid atha vā mṛgalipsayā
english: Devayānī said: "For what purpose have you come to this place, O king — to gather lotus-flowers, or out of desire for game?"

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca mṛgalipsur ahaṃ bhadre pānīyārtham upāgataḥ bahu cāpy anuyukto 'smi tan mānujñātum arhasi
english: Yayāti said: "I came seeking game and water, O noble lady. I have also been much engaged in duties — please grant me leave of that."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca dvābhyāṃ kanyāsahasrābhyāṃ dāsyā śarmiṣṭhayā saha tvadadhīnāsmi bhadraṃ te sakhā bhartā ca me bhava
english: Devayānī said: "Along with two thousand maidens and with my servant Śarmiṣṭhā, I am dependent on you. Blessings on you — be my companion and husband."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca viddhy auśanasi bhadraṃ te na tvām arho 'smi bhāmini avivāhyā hi rājāno devayāni pitus tava
english: Yayāti said: "Know me, O daughter of Uśanas, blessings on you — I am not worthy of you, O passionate one. For kings are not fit to be wedded by those of your father's lineage."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca saṃsṛṣṭaṃ brahmaṇā kṣatraṃ kṣatraṃ ca brahmasaṃhitam ṛṣiś ca ṛṣiputraś ca nāhuṣāṅga vahasva mām
english: Devayānī said: "The brahmin is mingled with the kshatriya and the kshatriya is joined with the brahmin; a seer and a seer's son — O Nāhuṣa, therefore take me in marriage."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca ekadehodbhavā varṇāś catvāro 'pi varāṅgane pṛthagdharmāḥ pṛthakśaucās teṣāṃ tu brāhmaṇo varaḥ
english: Yayāti said: "Though the four varṇas are born from one body, O finest of women, they have separate dharmas and separate purities, and among them the brahmin is supreme."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca pāṇidharmo nāhuṣāyaṃ na pumbhiḥ sevitaḥ purā taṃ me tvam agrahīr agre vṛṇomi tvām ahaṃ tataḥ
english: Devayānī said: "This rite of taking the hand, O Nāhuṣa, has not been observed by men before — you were the first to take my hand, therefore I choose you."

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu me manasvinyāḥ pāṇim anyaḥ pumān spṛśet gṛhītam ṛṣiputreṇa svayaṃ vāpy ṛṣiṇā tvayā
english: "How could any other man touch my hand — mine, a woman of spirit — after it has been taken by you, a seer's son, or rather by you who are yourself a seer?"

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca kruddhād āśīviṣāt sarpāj jvalanāt sarvatomukhāt durādharṣataro vipraḥ puruṣeṇa vijānatā
english: Yayāti said: "To a man who knows, a brahmin is more difficult to assail than an enraged venomous serpent or an all-consuming fire."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca katham āśīviṣāt sarpāj jvalanāt sarvatomukhāt durādharṣataro vipra ity āttha puruṣarṣabha
english: Devayānī said: "Why do you say a brahmin is more difficult to assail than a venomous serpent or an all-consuming fire, O bull among men?"

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca ekam āśīviṣo hanti śastreṇaikaś ca vadhyate hanti vipraḥ sarāṣṭrāṇi purāṇy api hi kopitaḥ
english: Yayāti said: "A venomous serpent kills one; one can be slain by a weapon — but an enraged brahmin destroys entire kingdoms and their cities."

sanskrit: durādharṣataro vipras tasmād bhīru mato mama ato 'dattāṃ ca pitrā tvāṃ bhadre na vivahāmy aham
english: "Therefore a brahmin is more difficult to assail, so I believe, O timid one — and for this reason, O noble lady, I will not marry you without your being given by your father."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca dattāṃ vahasva pitrā māṃ tvaṃ hi rājan vṛto mayā ayācato bhayaṃ nāsti dattāṃ ca pratigṛhṇataḥ
english: Devayānī said: "Take me as given by my father, O king — for you have been chosen by me. There is no fear for one who accepts a woman given freely."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tvaritaṃ devayānyātha preṣitaṃ pitur ātmanaḥ śrutvaiva ca sa rājānaṃ darśayām āsa bhārgavaḥ
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Then Devayānī quickly sent word to her father; and upon hearing it, the descendant of Bhṛgu presented the king before him.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva cāgataṃ śukraṃ yayātiḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ vavande brāhmaṇaṃ kāvyaṃ prāñjaliḥ praṇataḥ sthitaḥ
english: Seeing Śukra arrived, Yayāti, lord of the earth, bowed to that brahmin, the descendant of Kavi, standing with folded hands in reverence.

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca rājāyaṃ nāhuṣas tāta durge me pāṇim agrahīt namas te dehi mām asmai nānyaṃ loke patiṃ vṛṇe
english: Devayānī said: "This king, the son of Nahuṣa, took my hand in an inaccessible place, father. I bow to you — give me to him; I choose no other husband in the world."

sanskrit: śukra uvāca vṛto 'nayā patir vīra sutayā tvaṃ mameṣṭayā gṛhāṇemāṃ mayā dattāṃ mahiṣīṃ nahuṣātmaja
english: Śukra said: "You have been chosen as husband by this daughter of mine whom I hold dear, O hero. Take her, given by me as your queen, O son of Nahuṣa."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca adharmo na spṛśed evaṃ mahān mām iha bhārgava varṇasaṃkarajo brahmann iti tvāṃ pravṛṇomy aham
english: Yayāti said: "Let no great transgression touch me here, O descendant of Bhṛgu — it is due to the sin born of mingling of varṇas that I appeal to you thus, O brahmin."

sanskrit: śukra uvāca adharmāt tvāṃ vimuñcāmi varayasva yathepṣitam asmin vivāhe mā glāsīr ahaṃ pāpaṃ nudāmi te
english: Śukra said: "I release you from the transgression — choose as you desire. Do not despair in this marriage; I remove the sin from you."

sanskrit: vahasva bhāryāṃ dharmeṇa devayānīṃ sumadhyamām anayā saha saṃprītim atulāṃ samavāpsyasi
english: "Take the slender-waisted Devayānī as your wife according to dharma; together with her you will attain incomparable joy."

sanskrit: iyaṃ cāpi kumārī te śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī saṃpūjyā satataṃ rājan mā caināṃ śayane hvayeḥ
english: "And this maiden Śarmiṣṭhā, daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, should always be honored by you, O king — but never summon her to your bed."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam ukto yayātis tu śukraṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam jagāma svapuraṃ hṛṣṭo anujñāto mahātmanā
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Thus addressed, Yayāti circumambulated Śukra and departed for his own city with joy, having received leave from that great-souled one.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yayātiḥ svapuraṃ prāpya mahendrapurasaṃnibham praviśyāntaḥpuraṃ tatra devayānīṃ nyaveśayat
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Yayāti reached his own city, resembling the city of great Indra, and entering the inner apartments, he installed Devayānī there.

sanskrit: devayānyāś cānumate tāṃ sutāṃ vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ aśokavanikābhyāśe gṛhaṃ kṛtvā nyaveśayat
english: With Devayānī's consent, he had a house built near the aśoka grove and installed there that daughter of Vṛṣaparvan.

sanskrit: vṛtāṃ dāsīsahasreṇa śarmiṣṭhām āsurāyaṇīm vāsobhir annapānaiś ca saṃvibhajya susatkṛtām
english: Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of the asura line, attended by a thousand maidservants, was provided with garments, food, and drink, and treated with great honor.

sanskrit: devayānyā tu sahitaḥ sa nṛpo nahuṣātmajaḥ vijahāra bahūn abdān devavan mudito bhṛśam
english: Together with Devayānī, that king, son of Nahuṣa, sported for many years, greatly delighted like a god.

sanskrit: ṛtukāle tu saṃprāpte devayānī varāṅganā lebhe garbhaṃ prathamataḥ kumāraṃ ca vyajāyata
english: When the proper season came, Devayānī, that finest of women, conceived first and gave birth to a son.

sanskrit: gate varṣasahasre tu śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī dadarśa yauvanaṃ prāptā ṛtuṃ sā cānvacintayat
english: When a thousand years had passed, Śarmiṣṭhā, daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, reaching the bloom of youth, saw that her season had come and reflected thus:

sanskrit: ṛtukālaś ca saṃprāpto na ca me 'sti patir vṛtaḥ kiṃ prāptaṃ kiṃ nu kartavyaṃ kiṃ vā kṛtvā kṛtaṃ bhavet
english: "The season has arrived, and yet I have no husband chosen for me. What has been gained? What must be done? What, if done, would be truly done?"

sanskrit: devayānī prajātāsau vṛthāhaṃ prāptayauvanā yathā tayā vṛto bhartā tathaivāhaṃ vṛṇomi tam
english: "Devayānī has borne a child, while I, having attained youth, am barren. As she chose her husband, so I too shall choose him."

sanskrit: rājñā putraphalaṃ deyam iti me niścitā matiḥ apīdānīṃ sa dharmātmā iyān me darśanaṃ rahaḥ
english: "It is my firm resolve that the king must grant me the fruit of a son. Would that this righteous-souled one might come to me now in private."

sanskrit: atha niṣkramya rājāsau tasmin kāle yadṛcchayā aśokavanikābhyāśe śarmiṣṭhāṃ prāpya viṣṭhitaḥ
english: Then, at that very time, the king came out by chance and encountered Śarmiṣṭhā standing near the aśoka grove.

sanskrit: tam ekaṃ rahite dṛṣṭvā śarmiṣṭhā cāruhāsinī pratyudgamyāñjaliṃ kṛtvā rājānaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Seeing him alone in a secluded spot, the lovely-smiling Śarmiṣṭhā went forward, made the anjali gesture, and spoke these words to the king:

sanskrit: somasyendrasya viṣṇor vā yamasya varuṇasya vā tava vā nāhuṣa kule kaḥ striyaṃ spraṣṭum arhati
english: "In the lineage of Soma, Indra, Viṣṇu, Yama, or Varuṇa — or in yours, O Nāhuṣa — who would be worthy to touch a woman?"

sanskrit: rūpābhijanaśīlair hi tvaṃ rājan vettha māṃ sadā sā tvāṃ yāce prasādyāham ṛtuṃ dehi narādhipa
english: "For you, O king, have always known me by my beauty, lineage, and conduct. I, propitiating you, ask you — grant me the season's gift, O lord of men."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca vedmi tvāṃ śīlasaṃpannāṃ daityakanyām aninditām rūpe ca te na paśyāmi sūcyagram api ninditam
english: Yayāti said: "I know you as a maiden of the daitya race endowed with good conduct and without reproach; in your beauty I see not even a needle's point of fault."

sanskrit: abravīd uśanā kāvyo devayānīṃ yadāvaham neyam āhvayitavyā te śayane vārṣaparvaṇī
english: "Yet Uśanas Kāvya told me when he entrusted Devayānī to me: 'This daughter of Vṛṣaparvan must never be summoned to your bed.'"

sanskrit: śarmiṣṭhovāca na narmayuktaṃ vacanaṃ hinasti; na strīṣu rājan na vivāhakāle prāṇātyaye sarvadhanāpahāre; pañcānṛtāny āhur apātakāni
english: Śarmiṣṭhā said: "Words spoken in jest do not harm; nor do those spoken to women, O king, nor at the time of marriage, nor when life is at stake, nor when all one's wealth is being taken — these five kinds of untruth are said to be without sin."

sanskrit: pṛṣṭaṃ tu sākṣye pravadantam anyathā; vadanti mithyopahitaṃ narendra ekārthatāyāṃ tu samāhitāyāṃ; mithyā vadantam anṛtaṃ hinasti
english: "But one who speaks falsely when questioned as a witness, or one who is falsely accused — they say, O lord of men, that in a matter rightly and wholly agreed upon, falsehood does not harm the speaker of untruth."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca rājā pramāṇaṃ bhūtānāṃ sa naśyeta mṛṣā vadan arthakṛcchram api prāpya na mithyā kartum utsahe
english: Yayāti said: "A king is the measure of all beings; he would perish by speaking falsehood. Even in financial distress I am not inclined to act falsely."

sanskrit: śarmiṣṭhovāca samāv etau matau rājan patiḥ sakhyāś ca yaḥ patiḥ samaṃ vivāham ity āhuḥ sakhyā me 'si patir vṛtaḥ
english: Śarmiṣṭhā said: "These two are considered equal, O king: a husband and the husband of a companion. Marriage to both is called equal — you have been chosen as husband by my companion, so you are my husband too."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca dātavyaṃ yācamānebhya iti me vratam āhitam tvaṃ ca yācasi māṃ kāmaṃ brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te
english: Yayāti said: "My vow is established that I must give to those who ask. You are asking me — speak your desire, what shall I do for you?"

sanskrit: śarmiṣṭhovāca adharmāt trāhi māṃ rājan dharmaṃ ca pratipādaya tvatto 'patyavatī loke careyaṃ dharmam uttamam
english: Śarmiṣṭhā said: "Protect me from unrighteousness, O king, and establish dharma for me — having offspring from you, I could practice the highest dharma in the world."

sanskrit: traya evādhanā rājan bhāryā dāsas tathā sutaḥ yat te samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya tad dhanam
english: "There are three who own no wealth, O king: the wife, the slave, and the son — whatever they acquire belongs to him to whom they belong."

sanskrit: devayānyā bhujiṣyāsmi vaśyā ca tava bhārgavī sā cāhaṃ ca tvayā rājan bharaṇīye bhajasva mām
english: "I am a maidservant of Devayānī and subject to the descendant of Bhṛgu, and so am I also within your care, O king — therefore take me as one whom you must support."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu rājā sa tathyam ity eva jajñivān pūjayām āsa śarmiṣṭhāṃ dharmaṃ ca pratyapādayat
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Thus addressed, the king recognized this as true and honored Śarmiṣṭhā, fulfilling dharma for her.

sanskrit: samāgamya ca śarmiṣṭhāṃ yathākāmam avāpya ca anyonyam abhisaṃpūjya jagmatus tau yathāgatam
english: Having come together with Śarmiṣṭhā and satisfied their desires, they honored one another and departed each the way they had come.

sanskrit: tasmin samāgame subhrūḥ śarmiṣṭhā cāruhāsinī lebhe garbhaṃ prathamatas tasmān nṛpatisattamāt
english: From that union, the fair-browed, lovely-smiling Śarmiṣṭhā first conceived from that best of kings.

sanskrit: prajajñe ca tataḥ kāle rājan rājīvalocanā kumāraṃ devagarbhābhaṃ rājīvanibhalocanam
english: And in due time, O king, the lotus-eyed one gave birth to a son resembling the offspring of a god, with eyes like lotus petals.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvā kumāraṃ jātaṃ tu devayānī śucismitā cintayām āsa duḥkhārtā śarmiṣṭhāṃ prati bhārata
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Hearing that a son had been born, the pure-smiling Devayānī became distressed and began to reflect regarding Śarmiṣṭhā, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: abhigamya ca śarmiṣṭhāṃ devayāny abravīd idam kim idaṃ vṛjinaṃ subhru kṛtaṃ te kāmalubdhayā
english: And approaching Śarmiṣṭhā, Devayānī said: "What is this wrong that you have done, O fair-browed one, overcome by desire?"

sanskrit: śarmiṣṭhovāca ṛṣir abhyāgataḥ kaś cid dharmātmā vedapāragaḥ sa mayā varadaḥ kāmaṃ yācito dharmasaṃhitam
english: Śarmiṣṭhā said: "Some sage of righteous soul, master of the Vedas, came as a guest. He who grants boons was asked by me for the desire in accordance with dharma."

sanskrit: nāham anyāyataḥ kāmam ācarāmi śucismite tasmād ṛṣer mamāpatyam iti satyaṃ bravīmi te
english: "I do not act upon desire unjustly, O pure-smiling one. This offspring of mine is from that sage — this I tell you truly."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca śobhanaṃ bhīru satyaṃ ced atha sa jñāyate dvijaḥ gotranāmābhijanato vettum icchāmi taṃ dvijam
english: Devayānī said: "Very well, O timid one, if it is true — then let that brahmin be identified. I wish to know that twice-born man by his lineage, name, and family."

sanskrit: śarmiṣṭhovāca ojasā tejasā caiva dīpyamānaṃ raviṃ yathā taṃ dṛṣṭvā mama saṃpraṣṭuṃ śaktir nāsīc chucismite
english: Śarmiṣṭhā said: "Blazing with energy and splendor like the sun — upon seeing him, I had no power to question him, O pure-smiling one."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca yady etad evaṃ śarmiṣṭhe na manyur vidyate mama apatyaṃ yadi te labdhaṃ jyeṣṭhāc chreṣṭhāc ca vai dvijāt
english: Devayānī said: "If that is so, Śarmiṣṭhā, then I harbor no anger — if you have obtained offspring from a brahmin who is both the eldest and the best."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca anyonyam evam uktvā ca saṃprahasya ca te mithaḥ jagāma bhārgavī veśma tathyam ity eva jajñuṣī
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Having thus spoken to one another and laughed together, the daughter of Bhṛgu returned home, accepting it as true.
